title: Goodwin learns ukulele, then banjo, influenced by Banjo Joe
summary: Goodwin disliked school music, taught himself ukulele as a teenager, then took banjo lessons, first imitating Banjo Joe.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Actually in school in my primary grades, well I didn't like music. I had all kinds of things against music, you know, but a couple of times I wished I could go and hide when we had this elementary music where you had to write down a note and do all this. I'd want to go and hide. I just didn't like music; that is, to learn it, you know, but after I became a teenager, well I got interested in music through
Oh, I was about to ask how you got on the guitar/.
Well, I started playing the ukelele and I --
-- became very adept with the ukelele. I could play the melody and all --

No, I taught myself to play ukelele. I bought a little book and I learned the chords and the single notes and from what little music training I'd had in school, well I could go along with this but when I bought the banjo it was a different story. I had to take some lessons because it was a musical instrument. The ukelele was just a little thing you play around with, however, now you can get a lot of music out of a ukelele if you know how.
Well, I'm going to ask you a question. Who influenced you on banjo and guitar playing; through records and who's your favorite?
The fellow that influenced me was a guy that was playing with Benny Moten, a guy called Banjo Joe.
Was this on banjo or guitar?
On banjo, and I had known him since

early childhood. He was -- actually I knew him in my daddy's Leavenworth, home in Kansas and I knew him then as a mandolin player. He played mandolin but his style of banjo playing was similar to a mandolin, but I did like his style but then when I did start playing guitar, learning guitar rather, well I began to hear guys that were more great, I would think, you know, and their styles were different and I became sort of confused on which way to go.
I might still be confused, for all I know, but the thing about it, it was a thing that I got away from his style and I'm happy I did because it was --
